name: DP Basics
description: Dynamic programming stores answers to repeated subproblems so they are solved once.
commonMistakes: Using DP when the subproblems do not overlap
Not defining the state clearly

name: Memoization
description: Top-down DP uses recursion plus a cache to avoid recomputation.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to store computed results
Using a memo table with the wrong dimensions

name: Tabulation
description: Bottom-up DP fills a table in dependency order without recursion.
exampleJava: for (int i = 2; i <= n; i++) dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2];
commonMistakes: Filling states before their dependencies are ready
Misaligning array indices with the mathematical state

name: State Transition
description: Each DP state should be derived from smaller well-defined previous states.
commonMistakes: Skipping a valid choice in the recurrence
Mixing state meaning across indices

name: Space Optimization
description: When only recent states are needed, replace a full DP table with rolling variables or rows.
exampleJava: int prev2 = 0, prev1 = 1; int cur = prev1 + prev2;
commonMistakes: Overwriting a state before it is used
Optimizing space before understanding the original recurrence

name: Grid DP
description: Use row-column states when movement is constrained across a matrix or board.
commonMistakes: Ignoring blocked cells or boundaries
Using the wrong base row or base column initialization

name: Knapsack Style DP
description: Model take-or-skip choices over items and capacities or target sums.
commonMistakes: Updating 1D DP in the wrong direction
Using capacity states that go negative

name: Sequence DP
description: Track the best sequence ending at each position under an ordering rule.
commonMistakes: Allowing invalid sequence extensions
Forgetting to initialize each dp[i] to 1

name: String DP
description: Build DP over prefixes or suffixes of strings to compare, align, or match characters.
commonMistakes: Confusing indices of the string with indices of the dp table
Forgetting the extra 0th row and column

name: Interval DP
description: Solve subproblems on contiguous ranges and combine splits or inward moves.
exampleJava: dp[i][j] = Math.min(dp[i][j], cost(i, k, j) + dp[i][k] + dp[k + 1][j]);
commonMistakes: Iterating intervals in the wrong order
Not choosing a correct split variable

name: Variable-Jump Cost DP
description: Minimize total cost when each position can be reached from several earlier positions with jump-dependent transition cost.
exampleJava: for (int jump = 1; jump <= k && i - jump >= 0; jump++) best = Math.min(best, dp[i - jump] + Math.abs(h[i] - h[i - jump]));
commonMistakes: Checking only one previous state when several jump lengths are allowed
Forgetting to guard indices when exploring larger jumps

name: Jump-Memory Reachability DP
description: Track whether a state is reachable when the next moves depend on both the current position and the previous jump length.
exampleJava: for (int prevJump : reachable.get(stone)) { for (int next = prevJump - 1; next <= prevJump + 1; next++) { ... } }
commonMistakes: Tracking only the stone index and forgetting the last jump length
Allowing zero or negative jump lengths as valid next states

name: Cooldown State DP
description: Track multiple states such as holding, selling, or resting when an action changes what is legal on the next step.
exampleJava: nextHold = Math.max(hold, rest - price); nextSold = hold + price; nextRest = Math.max(rest, sold);
commonMistakes: Updating states in-place without preserving the previous day values
Ignoring that selling today affects whether buying is allowed tomorrow

name: Probability DP
description: Store probabilities instead of boolean or integer counts when a state branches into weighted outcomes.
commonMistakes: Using integer division instead of floating point probability accumulation
Forgetting to drop moves that leave the board

name: Transaction-State DP
description: Represent stock or trading problems with state dimensions for day, holding status, and remaining transaction budget.
commonMistakes: Using the wrong transition when a sell should consume a transaction
Collapsing holding and not-holding states into one value

name: Resource-Budget DP
description: Track a position state together with remaining removals, energy, or operations budget when the best decision depends on both.
commonMistakes: Tracking only the grid cell and forgetting how much budget remains
Using transitions that overspend the allowed resource budget

name: Segment-Merge DP
description: Store compact boundary DP states for array segments so point updates and segment merges preserve the global optimal answer.
commonMistakes: Merging child segments without tracking whether the touching boundary elements were selected
Using a segment summary that is too weak to support point updates
